questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Vrije University is renowned for their neuroscience programs, which was a big part of my choosing this destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The VU is incredibly helpful with giving you all the necessary information and is quick to reply should you need anything additionally. They send out emails leading up to your exchange with all the required information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails with all necessary information, and an introduction week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Use DUWO housing!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is almost impossible to find an apartment on your own in Amsterdam - they are having quite the housing crisis.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Again, as with the incoming student information, it was incredibly easy to register through their website for your courses. They also have great descriptions of them. I followed a minor which is essentially a course-package you can pick, whereas if you were to pick individual courses it is a bit more difficult as you have to make sure they do not overlap timespot wise.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had trouble with registering for one course I really wanted and emailed their international student email address and they registered me for the course within one day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read all the course descriptions - they are very helpful, and follow a minor if there is one of interest to you - makes your life a lot easier.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found it quite a bit easier than UCPH. I followed a minor, and I only had multiple-choice exams and some group projects. The actual level of teaching was still quite high though, and there were sone very interesting lectures.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More group projects, less difficult exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Neuronal networks and behaviour, the adaptive brain, experimental cell biology I and II, and molecular principles of brain disorders.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Neuronal networks and behaviour and molecular principles of brain disorders. Experimental cell biology I and II are a review of most intro-level human biology courses given at UCPH. The adaptive brain was also interesting, but they have recently changed the structure of their laboratory practicals and foregone an actual, in-person, lab  990+260+530exercise, and they alternative was quite boring and chaotic (due to it being new).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a gym (with classes) and quite a couple of sports teams. They hosted quite a few social activities particularly in the introduction week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Participate in the intro week! It can be a bit cringe, but it is a great way to meet a lot of people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam has incredible museums, and a great jazz scene (Tuesday night jazz at Bimhuis is free and drinks are cheap!)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, Amsterdam and Copenhagen are very similar

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to your classmates, join a local sports team, go bar-hopping and challenge yourself and your international friends to speak with the locals you meet!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You have to get used to their chaotic biking (as opposed to CPH) :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Say yes to any cultural activity that comes your way - you won't regret it
Rent a car and drive around the north of Amsterdam and see the beaches and dunes there
They have great thrifting (clothes) opportunities --> cheaper and better for environment!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: n/a

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I met there

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Prioritising your time and the things you want to do

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
